channel.title: Twinthos Notes
channel.description: Plain-English, sourced writing about what AI actually does to a small business: the job, the money, the record, and who answers for it.

item.title: What a digital employee really costs over three years
item.description: The monthly fee is the smallest number in the deal. Setup, the approver, every failure and the exit sit outside it. Here is the whole three-year sum.

item.title: Chatbot or digital employee? What you are actually buying
item.description: A chatbot answers what you ask and forgets you. A digital employee does one job, remembers your rules and keeps a record. Here is the gap, and the money.

item.title: 14 questions to ask before you buy a managed AI agent
item.description: A short list to take into the meeting. Every question has an answer you want and a reply that should worry you. Hear two worrying replies and you walk.

item.title: Did the cash machine really kill the bank teller?
item.description: Everyone says cash machines killed bank teller jobs. US figures show teller numbers rising for 25 years after the ATM arrived, and what that means now.

item.title: What an AI employee really costs per hour
item.description: The tokens cost tens of dollars a month. The monthly fee is the visible part. The number that decides it is the time your team spends checking the work.

item.title: What is AI, and what can it actually do for you?
item.description: A plain-English guide for anyone who has never used AI. What it is, the three ways it changes an ordinary week, and what to hand over first.

item.title: 53% of small firms already let AI cover a full job
item.description: A survey of 729 owners found 53% let AI absorb a full-time role's workload, and nobody in the data was let go. The 65% who are tired kept the checking.

item.title: The US renamed AI to SI. Your work is exactly the same
item.description: On 29 September 2026 US agencies were told to say super intelligence, not AI. What changed for a small business: the name, not the work or the questions.

item.title: What answering your phone with software really costs
item.description: Google's Gemini 4 Argon is $2 per million input tokens. Here is what 600 answered enquiries cost in a month, and what still breaks when you switch it on.

item.title: What an AI agent actually does, and how to spot a fake
item.description: Four big firms shipped agents this autumn. Here is what makes one a real digital employee, and how to tell in ten minutes what you are being sold.

item.title: Why most AI projects fail before they start
item.description: MIT found about 95% of generative AI pilots made no measurable difference to profit. The 5% that worked fixed the paperwork before they bought anything.

item.title: Why the same customer gets two different answers
item.description: Dell, SAP, Google, Meta and Workday all announced company memory in eight days. Your staff still spend 2.3 hours a week retyping what the business knows.

item.title: 88% of firms use AI, but scaled agents are rare
item.description: Stanford's 2026 AI Index: 88% of organisations use AI, yet scaled AI agents sit in single digits. The adoption gap, the data behind it and its limits.

item.title: Entry-level jobs and AI in 2026: what the data shows
item.description: Stanford's August 2026 update: workers aged 22 to 25 in AI-exposed jobs are 19% below trend, from fewer hires, not layoffs. What it shows and what it does not.

item.title: US horses and tractors, 1900 to 1960: what the data says
item.description: US farm horses and mules peaked at 26.7 million in 1918 and fell to about 3 million by 1960. The tractor took four decades, and freed 88 million acres.

item.title: 11 hours a week on admin: the cost to a UK small business
item.description: A July 2026 Amex survey says UK owners spend 11 hours a week on admin. What that costs per year, a calculator for your own week, and how far to trust the number.

item.title: 170 million jobs created, 92 million lost by 2030
item.description: The WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025 projects 170 million new roles and 92 million displaced by 2030, a net gain of 78 million, and 11 in 100 workers left behind.

item.title: How to tell if your AI agent is being used against you
item.description: Prompt injection, data exfiltration and agent collusion are not science fiction. Here is what they look like in practice, and how to spot them.

item.title: Why AI agents need security audits before you switch them on
item.description: A real AI agent has permissions, memory and a log. That means it also has an attack surface. Here is what to check before it goes live.

item.title: AI security audit checklist: 10 things to verify before your agent goes live
item.description: A practical checklist for securing AI agents before deployment. Covers permissions, logging, MCP config, prompt injection, CISA KEV, EPSS and more.

item.title: What the Langflow CVSS 9.9 exploit teaches us about AI agent security
item.description: Langflow's MCP stdio transport had a CVSS 9.9 RCE flaw. Here is what happened, what it means for AI agents, and how to prevent it in your stack.

item.title: The MCP security gap most vendors won't mention
item.description: MCP servers connect AI agents to your data. Most vendors treat them as plumbing. They are not. Here is the risk and what to do about it.
